verses.commentary: Amos, a shepherd from Tekoa in Judah, receives visions about the northern kingdom. Not a professional prophet but a farmer called by God. The earthquake mentioned was so catastrophic it became a dating marker (Zechariah 14:5). Two years of warning before devastation.

The Lord roars from Zion. Not Bethel or Dan where Israel worships, but Jerusalem, the true sanctuary. When God roars, nature withers. Carmel, the lush mountain, dries up. Creation responds to the Creator's anger.

For three sins, even for four. A rhetorical pattern: the cup overflows. Damascus, capital of Aram, judged first. They threshed Gilead with iron sledges. Brutal warfare against Israel's territory east of Jordan. God notices cruelty between nations.
Fire on the house of Hazael. The dynasty that oppressed Israel will burn. Ben-Hadad's fortresses consumed. What they built through violence will fall through judgment.
The gate of Damascus broken. Exile to Kir, their place of origin (9:7). They end where they began. God reverses their history.
Gaza, chief Philistine city, judged for slave trading. They took whole communities, selling them to Edom. Human trafficking provokes divine wrath. Commerce in people is commerce in souls.
Fire on the walls of Gaza. The fortresses that protected slave markets will burn. Walls cannot protect wickedness from God.
Ashdod, Ashkelon, Ekron. The Philistine pentapolis systematically dismantled. The last of the Philistines will die. Total judgment on a trafficking nation.
Tyre, the merchant city, sold captives to Edom. They disregarded a treaty of brotherhood, a covenant between nations. Broken covenants bring broken cities. God holds nations to their treaties.
Fire on the walls of Tyre. The great trading center will burn. Commercial success cannot buy immunity from justice.

Edom pursued his brother with a sword. Jacob and Esau's descendants, locked in perpetual hatred. Anger raged continually. Fury that never cools, vengeance that never satisfies. Brother against brother across centuries.
Fire on Teman and Bozrah. Edom's cities burn. Perpetual hatred meets perpetual fire. What they would not release, releases them.
Ammon ripped open pregnant women of Gilead. War atrocities to extend borders. Land expansion through murder of the unborn. God sees what armies do in darkness.
Fire on Rabbah. The Ammonite capital falls amid war cries and storms. The violence they dealt returns in judgment. Violent winds echo their violence.
The king and officials go into exile together. Leadership that led to atrocity now leads to captivity. Shared guilt, shared judgment.
